Personal introduction Â· Part 1

A little about me

The person behind these pages cannot be summarized by one label. This introduction gives the reader a starting point: where I come from, what matters to me, and what I hope to understand about myself.

My introduction

Hello! My name is Alexander T. Camino Jr.. I am a first-year college student taking Bachelor of Science in Information Systems (BSIS) from the Philippines. The people and experiences that have shaped me most are my family, because they inspire and support me and give me the strength to continue my studies.

People who know me might describe me as kind, patient, and responsible. I feel most like myself when I am with my family and friends, studying, or doing the things I enjoy. One thing I am proud of is continuing to work hard in my studies, because it taught me perseverance, diligence, and not giving up despite challenges.

I created this portfolio to look at the different parts of my identity with greater care. I want to understand how my physical self, sexuality, possessions, spirituality, political self, and digital life connect. Right now, I am learning to improve my programming skills and learn more about using technology. By the end of this reflection, I hope to understand myself better, recognize my strengths and weaknesses, and become a better person.

Respect — I listen to others’ opinions and treat my parents, teachers, and friends with courtesy.
Playing online games and using a computer — I enjoy these activities because they entertain me and help me learn new things about technology.
Programming and communication skills — I am learning to create computer programs and communicate more effectively with others.
Make the introduction sound like you. You can omit identifying details you would rather keep private.

Lesson 6 Â· Physical Self Â· Activity 1

The body that carries my story

My physical self is more than an image. My body lets me move through ordinary days, care for people, learn, rest, and experience the world. This reflection makes space for appreciation without demanding that I look a certain way.

My creative self-portrait

This photograph represents my physical self in a quiet countryside setting. The green field and open sky connect this portrait to a peaceful moment in my life.

Caption: I am still in the process of becoming a better version of myself and planning my future, but I know that one day I will live the life I have always prayed for.

Five Features That Make Me Unique

These may be visible features, mannerisms, sensory experiences, or abilities. Describe them neutrally and respectfully; uniqueness does not have to mean fitting a beauty standard.

My eyes allow me to observe the world, notice small details, and appreciate the beauty around me.
My smile represents my happiness and helps me express kindness and positivity toward other people.
My hand gestures and facial expressions help me communicate my thoughts and feelings confidently.
My body gives me strength, energy, and the ability to perform daily activities while learning new things.
My laughter is something unique to me. It reflects my personality and brings happiness to the people around me.

Three ways I care for my physical well-being

  1. Movement: I take short walks and stretch between study sessions or after spending time at the computer.
  2. Rest and nourishment: I try to drink water throughout the day, eat regular meals, and get enough sleep so I have energy for school.
  3. Health and kindness: I take breaks from screens, listen to my body when I feel tired, and give myself time to rest.

Reflection Â· seeing and appreciating my physical self

How do I see and appreciate my physical self?

I appreciate my hands because they help me write, study, and use a computer to learn programming. My feelings about my appearance can change, but I remind myself that my body is valuable for all it helps me do.

How has society or social media influenced how I perceive my body?

Social media can make me compare my appearance with edited photos and unrealistic beauty standards. I remind myself that images may use filters and do not show the whole person, so I try not to judge my worth by online posts.

What can I do to develop a healthier relationship with my appearance?

I can build a healthier relationship with my appearance by limiting comparison online and speaking to myself with respect. I will focus on caring for my body and appreciating what it allows me to do.

Lesson 7 Â· Sexual Self Â· Activity 2

Knowing myself, respecting myself

Sexuality is a personal dimension of identity and well-being. This values map focuses on self-understanding, dignity, boundaries, consent, and respectful relationships. Share only what feels appropriate for a class portfolio.

My four-part values map

Fill each part with words, short reflections, symbols, or illustrations. Your map may describe values and boundaries without disclosing private experiences or labels.

01 Â· Self-awareness

What have I learned about my sexuality and personal identity?

I understand that my identity is personal and can continue to develop as I learn about myself. I value respect, safety, and being true to my values. I will give myself time to understand who I am without pressure to share more than I feel comfortable sharing.

02 Â· Self-respect

How do I demonstrate respect for myself?

I respect myself by listening to my feelings, setting boundaries, and making thoughtful choices. I can seek reliable information and talk with a trusted adult when I have questions.

03 Â· Personal boundaries

What boundaries protect my dignity and well-being?

I want to protect my privacy, personal space, and time, including what I share online. I can state my boundary calmly and clearly, such as, “I am not comfortable sharing that.”

04 Â· Healthy relationships

What qualities belong in a healthy, respectful relationship?

A healthy relationship includes respect, honesty, trust, and open communication. Both people should feel safe, listen to each other, respect consent, and be free to say no or change their mind.

My relationship values

  • Consent: Consent means everyone agrees freely, understands what they are agreeing to, and can change their mind at any time.
  • Communication: I can share my thoughts clearly, listen carefully, and give others time to answer without pressuring them.
  • Respect: A no, a pause, or a different opinion should be accepted calmly and without pressure.
  • Support: I can seek guidance from a trusted family member, teacher, school counselor, or reliable health education source.

A boundary I want to honor

I will not share personal photos or private information when I feel pressured. This boundary helps protect my privacy and safety. I can communicate it by saying, “I am not comfortable sharing that. Please respect my decision.”

â€œMy dignity and safety deserve care, including from me.â€
This section can be thoughtful without being intimate. Keep private details private, use respectful language, and focus on your principles and well-being.

Lesson 8 Â· Material Self Â· Activity 3

Beyond the things I own

Possessions can carry memory, connection, identity, and hope. The meaning is often in the story attached to an objectâ€”not in its price. These five objects offer a small window into my experiences and aspirations.

Five meaningful possessions

These photos show objects and keepsakes that connect to my family, friendships, learning, memories, and goals.

The family artwork and awards connect me to my family’s support and the communities where I have studied and served.
The car’s camera and dashboard remind me that technology can solve practical problems and inspire me to learn more in Information Systems.
My certificate and medal preserve the memory of the effort I put into earning academic recognition. I keep their meaning as a reminder that persistence matters.
The family artwork represents the familiar surroundings, care, and encouragement that help me feel connected to home.
My awards encourage me to continue my studies, build my skills, and work toward a successful future.

What my objects say about me

Looking across these objects, I notice the importance of family, friendship, education, and making time to appreciate life. The awards are especially meaningful because they represent effort and growth, while the everyday photos remind me that relationships and memories matter just as much. Together, they reflect values I want to keep: gratitude, perseverance, curiosity, and connection. My worth is not measured by what I own; what matters most is the people, choices, and experiences these things bring to mind.

Lesson 9 Â· Spiritual Self Â· Activity 4

The values that give my life meaning

My spiritual self is reflected in what I hold sacred, the principles I return to, and the sources of meaning and inner strength that help me keep going. This reflection can express religious faith, personal philosophy, connection to community or nature, or a combination.

My personal reflection board

Build a visual board with photographs, colors, symbols, drawings, or words. Use the prompts below as captions or design each one as its own panel.

My core values

Name five values that guide your decisions, then give a short example for each.

Respect — I listen to others and treat them with courtesy. · Responsibility — I take my studies and duties seriously. · Perseverance — I keep trying when a lesson or task is difficult. · Gratitude — I appreciate my family’s support and the opportunities I have. · Kindness — I try to be patient and considerate toward others.

My source of strength

What gives me hope or steadiness in difficult times?

My family gives me hope and strength. Their support reminds me that I am not alone, encourages me to continue my studies, and motivates me to keep working toward a better future.

My purpose

What gives my life meaning beyond getting through the day?

My life has meaning in the love I share with my family, the effort I put into my education, and the person I am becoming. I hope to build a stable future, use my Information Systems skills well, and be someone my family can be proud of.

My inner peace

Which practices help me become calm, grounded, or grateful?

I feel more grounded when I take a quiet break, spend time outdoors, listen to music, or talk with someone I trust. Remembering my family’s support also helps me feel grateful and calm.

I will uphold respect by listening before I respond, responsibility by doing my best in school and at home, perseverance by continuing when work feels difficult, gratitude by appreciating the people who support me, and kindness by treating others with patience. I will try to show these values through small, consistent choices each day.

Reflection Â· the principles I return to

When I have a difficult choice, I want to remember respect and responsibility. They matter because I want to treat people fairly and be dependable in my studies and relationships. When life feels uncertain, I can draw strength from my family’s support and the goals I am working toward. A small practice that brings me back to myself is taking a quiet break, reflecting on what matters, and returning to the next task one step at a time. These beliefs do not mean that I always have the answers; they help me keep asking what is kind, honest, and meaningful.

Lesson 10 Â· Political Self Â· Activity 5

My voice, my responsibility

My political self includes how I understand community life, whose needs I notice, and the ways I can take part in positive change. This advocacy poster chooses one issue and turns concern into practical, respectful action.

Youth advocacy poster

Every Young Person Deserves a Chance to Learn and Succeed
Equal access to quality education for every young person.
Education can open doors to skills, confidence, and future opportunities. Yet some young people face barriers such as the cost of school needs, limited learning resources, or difficult circumstances at home. Students need support and encouragement so they can continue learning and reach their potential.
My graduation and academic awards represent the effort I have put into learning and the encouragement that helped me keep going. They remind me that education can create new opportunities. I want other young people to have the support and chance to work toward their own goals too.
I will value my education by attending to my studies, continuing to build my skills, and encouraging classmates and younger students to keep learning. Starting this school year, I will share helpful study knowledge when I can and support a respectful, encouraging learning environment.

Three practical actions young people can take

  1. Learn and verify: I will learn about education opportunities and challenges from teachers, school announcements, and reliable sources before sharing information.
  2. Take part with others: I can encourage classmates, study with others, and join school activities that help students feel supported and included.
  3. Make a concrete contribution: I can share notes or study tips when appropriate, offer help respectfully, and ask a teacher or school leader how students can support learning in our community.
My poster's call to action: Support every learner. Share knowledge, encourage a classmate, and help make education a path open to all.
Keep the poster persuasive and fair: distinguish confirmed information from opinion, avoid stigmatizing people affected by an issue, and offer a constructive next step.

Lesson 11 Â· Digital Self Â· Activity 6

Behind the screen: who am I online?

My digital self is shaped by what I share, how I communicate, whose voices I amplify, and the traces I leave. A thoughtful digital identity map can help me protect my privacy while showing care for others.

My digital identity map

Make a visual map with â€œMe onlineâ€ in the center and connect it to the five areas below. Use general examples; never include passwords, private messages, account handles, or sensitive personal information.

01 Â· My online identity

How do I describe myself as a digital citizen?

Online, I want to be known as a respectful, responsible, and curious Information Systems student. I enjoy learning about technology and improving my skills, and I want my online presence to show that I am kind, thoughtful, and willing to learn.

02 Â· My digital footprint

What traces can my activity leave?

My posts, comments, likes, searches, and shared photos can create a lasting picture of me. Even a casual post may be saved or seen without its original context, so I want to share things I would be comfortable standing by later.

03 Â· My online behavior

How do I communicate and interact?

I try to communicate politely and patiently, even when someone has a different opinion. I can check my tone before replying, give credit when I use another person’s ideas, and avoid joining in on hurtful comments or arguments.

04 Â· My digital responsibility

How do I protect privacy and respect others?

I will use strong, unique passwords and privacy settings, be careful with unfamiliar links, and ask permission before sharing someone else’s photo or message. I will also check information with reliable sources before reposting it.

05 Â· My improvement plan

Which online habits should I build or change?

I will begin setting aside focused time to learn useful technology and programming skills. I will reduce aimless scrolling by taking screen breaks, and I will review my progress each week by noticing whether I practiced a skill and kept a healthier balance.

A pause before I post

My digital improvement plan

I will begin: Practicing a useful programming or technology skill for a little time each week.

I will reduce or stop: Scrolling without a purpose when I could be resting, studying, or spending time with family.

I will protect: My passwords, private information, and other people’s privacy by checking before I click or share.

I will review my progress by: Checking every Sunday whether I practiced a skill, took breaks, and used the internet responsibly.

Personal Growth Commitment Â· Part 8

A letter to my future self

This one-page letter brings the portfolio together. Write to the person you hope to become with honesty and encouragement. Name a direction, the choices that can move you toward it, and how you will respond when growth feels difficult.

November 12, 2026

Dear future me,

As I write this, I am a first-year Information Systems student learning more about myself and thinking about the future I want to build. This portfolio helped me notice that I am more than one part of myself. My physical self reminds me to appreciate what my body helps me do each day; my values around identity and relationships remind me to treat myself and others with respect. The objects I chose tell me that family, friendship, learning, and perseverance matter to me, and the values that ground me are respect, responsibility, gratitude, kindness, and faith in the effort I put into my goals.

The kind of person I aspire to become is someone who listens patiently, follows through on responsibilities, and keeps learning even when something is challenging. I hope that I will keep caring for my body by getting enough rest, drinking water, and taking breaks from screens, honoring my boundaries by protecting my privacy and speaking up when I feel uncomfortable, and treating others with kindness by listening and responding respectfully.

I also want to use my voice to encourage young people to value education and keep working toward their goals. In my digital life, I will try to protect personal information, check information before sharing it, and communicate with respect. These are not promises to be perfect. They are directions I can return to, one choice at a time.

When things get difficult, please remember that your family supports you and that progress comes from taking one step at a time. Ask for help from a trusted family member, teacher, or friend when you need it. If you make a mistake, take responsibility, learn what you can, and begin again. Progress may be slow, but every honest effort helps you grow and move closer to the future you hope for.

My commitments to my growth are to keep improving my Information Systems skills, take care of my health and balance, and show respect and kindness in my relationships. I will know I am practicing them when I make time to learn, look after my well-being, and become someone others can count on. I hope future me is proud—not because everything went according to plan, but because we kept choosing honesty, care, courage, and learning.

With patience and hope,

Alexander T. Camino Jr.

This letter reflects the personality and goals shared throughout my portfolio.

My commitments, made practical

I will practice programming or another Information Systems skill at least once each week.
I will care for my health by taking screen breaks and keeping a regular routine, with encouragement from my family.
I will treat people with respect and kindness each day, and notice my progress by reflecting on my choices at the end of the week.
